diffSummary: Three new packages: @uptimebuyer/observability (redaction, structured logger, closed-label metrics registry, W3C traceparent tracer, health registry, SLO tracker, alert rules, platform metrics), @uptimebuyer/resilience (token bucket, abortable bulkhead, deadlines, retry policy, byte bounds, model budget) and @uptimebuyer/operations (incident trace builder, platform signal collection, readiness checks, encryption posture). Migrations 0020-0023: FR-23 retention/legal hold/erasure with tombstones, spend and adjustment separation of duties, dual-approval policy governance over current and scheduled revisions. packages/data: erasure runner (retention sweep, privacy request execution), grace-bounded jti prune, broker worker context moved to the @uptimebuyer/data/broker subpath, FR-18 ledger record completeness. apps/api: instrumentation, authenticate-first with atomic failure-token reservation and a pre-auth gate (per-source /32 or /64, global cap, bounded queue, hard verification timeout), operator and webhook bulkheads, three-state readiness, a token-protected operations listener. Offline security tooling (ESLint SAST, dependency/license check, migration lint with checksum lock) in pnpm verify; requirement coverage report under docs/coverage.

The first green run surfaced only test-side mistakes (e7de62e: FR-23 checks assumed every observation has a raw body; catalog name[] cast; SoD guard test hit UB091; telemetry timed before binding; invalid provider kind; terminal order in a poll test; degraded-readiness pool too fast; T-055 stage order), corrected without loosening an assertion. Recovery policies (M11) are outside dualApprovalPolicyKeys for now (residual).
URL paths containing @ are treated as userinfo and redacted (fail safe).
Pre-auth sources are keyed IPv4 /32 and IPv6 /64; global pre-auth cap 256 with a 64-waiter, 2 s queue; hard verification timeout 10 s answered with the uniform 401.

securityReview: S1: unauthenticated webhook floods shared the operator bulkhead (red c815d45: operators shed with 429) -> separate webhook bulkhead (96173f0).
S2: a pre-scheduled AUTHORITY revision could switch dual approval off later (red e98a97b) -> enabling refused while an unreviewed future revision is queued (783887d).
S3: token-only URL userinfo not redacted (red 4221401) -> any userinfo sensitive (e36a917).
S4: redaction work grew with input size; multi-megabyte fields did not finish in 120 s (red 4221401) -> bounded scan window and bounded repetition (e36a917).
S5: dual approval decided from the current revision only (red 2cf0543: three governance cases) -> migration 0022 decides over current and every scheduled revision under the governance lock (16fb9d2).
S6: budget-credit SoD threshold used the original approval amount (red 985d234: all three cases) -> judged on credit and resulting limit, migration 0023 backstop (5159042).

S7: bulkhead slots leaked on early disconnects; anonymous traffic held operator capacity (red 0041eab: both 429) -> slots tied to response close, abortable queue, slots after authentication (cbb3282).
S8: quarantined callback deliveries looked like orphans and could be reopened (red aaf09d5: processed_at NULL) -> atomic delivery+job, terminal quarantine (ad44a69).

S9: truncation after shortening replacements let characters beyond the kept length shift in; straddling secrets half kept (red 2bdb4c9) -> matches located on original offsets, only offsets below the kept length emitted (23da2f4).
S10: userinfo stopped at / ? # (red 2bdb4c9: four cases) -> userinfo runs to the authority last @ (23da2f4).
S11: pre-auth verification unbounded after S7; limiter checked with has() (red 659ce91: 200 in flight, cap 8) -> atomic failure-token reservation, per-source and global caps (6edfd14).

S12: pre-auth slot freed on client close while verification kept running; no verification bound (red 825369c: 48 in flight with cap 8; hung verifier never freed) -> slot released once in finally, 10 s hard timeout (916f305).

S13: global cap let ten sources lock a legitimate operator out; IPv6 rotation in one /64 got 30 concurrent verifications (red 825369c) -> source keyed /32 and /64, global 256 configurable, bounded queue (916f305).
unresolvedRisks: A large distributed source pool (many /32s or /64s) can still saturate any in-process cap: the pre-auth caps, failure buckets and bulkheads bound one process work, they cannot distinguish a botnet from a busy customer base. The real mitigation is edge/WAF rate limiting in front of the API at deployment (M14 input).
Rate buckets, pre-auth caps and bulkheads are per process; multiple API replicas multiply capacity, and behind a proxy UB_TRUST_PROXY must be set or every client shares one source.
Verification work left running after the hard timeout is bounded only by the JWKS fetch timeout and database statement limits; its slot is already returned.
RLS is not enabled; tenant isolation remains composite keys plus server authorization (proven catalog-wide by T-053).
Recovery policies (M11) are not covered by dual approval.
Retention, jti prune and the other runners are unscheduled, so FR-23 retention does not happen in practice until M14 schedules them.
No step-up authentication for high-risk actions (needs IdP acr/auth_time).
The offline advisory list is empty and must be fed from a reviewed source; there is no online advisory check by design.
SLO and load numbers are local measurements, not production evidence.

truthStatement: M13 implemented and locally verified retention/legal hold/erasure, separation of duties, grace-bounded jti pruning, the broker context subpath, observability, resilience bounds, chaos recovery and offline security tooling against a throwaway PostgreSQL database with simulated sensors, a recorded-contract broker, a contract-fake CMMS and a loopback test identity provider. No deployment, real identity provider, provider, payment, production load, encryption-at-rest, penetration test or physical recovery evidence exists; all of it remains NOT_RUN, and the runners listed in nextModuleInputs are not scheduled.
